subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Recovery, Sleep, Hydration, and Injury Prevention
essentialQuestion: Why does what I do between sessions decide what happens in them?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of recovery as part of training rather than a reward for it in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe sleep and its effect on coordination, mood, and injury risk using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving warning signs of overuse and under-recovery; correct it and explain why.
Connect common activity injuries and how they are prevented with returning after illness or injury on a graded plan and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a recovery protocol for the learner’s own program, including the specific signals that will trigger a reduced or rest day, and a graded return-to-activity plan.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing a condition builds the protocol with guardian input around the constraints they already have.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
